Both are 0° built-in lean, so every word of the geometry in this section stands, including the 59-frame film measurement. Left unedited on purpose: a log records what was believed at the time. Full correction in the Aug 14 section at the top of this log.

sections.t: How this log works
sections.k: Anything worked through end to end lands here as one section, so the doing-plans stay short.
sections.b:
The rule going forward: when a question gets worked through properly — research, a claim checked, a decision reached — it lands here as ONE section rather than being spread through the plans that tell you what to do.

That keeps the split clean. The Routine plan, the Setup plan and the Distance Grind say what you do NOW, in as few words as they can. This log says how each of those instructions was arrived at, what was rejected on the way, and where the sources were. When an instruction changes, the reasoning does not have to be re-derived and it does not have to sit in the middle of a plan you read on the practice green.

Each section carries the same skeleton: the question, what checked out, what did not, what changed in the other plans, what remains unmeasured, and the sources. The unmeasured line is not optional — a workshop that cannot say what it still does not know is a sales pitch.

lesson.title: Groove the choke-down — and give 'a little' a number
lesson.body: The claw is out as of Sep 12 — your call, you hated it — and what you play on the short ones now is a conventional grip held DOWN the handle a little. What that does is standard and sound: a shorter lever makes a smaller stroke, puts your hands nearer the ball and takes weight out from under them, which is the right trade inside six feet where the ball only has to reach the hole on line. What it does NOT do is what the claw was for — your trail hand is back on the club, so quiet hands is a discipline again rather than a geometry, and the flick is something to watch for rather than something the grip prevents. The thing this drill exists to settle is the word 'a little'. An unmeasured grip height drifts, and because distance comes from stroke length at a fixed tempo, a drifting choke is a pace variable hiding inside a line fix — on the one fault that is already open. Mark it, then hold it.
lesson.drill: Mark the handle, then two blocks of ten at five feet — both choked to the mark, one normal stroke, one pop.
steps: FIRST, THE MARK. Set up as you would on a five-footer and note where your lead hand sits — a band of tape, or measure down from the butt in inches and write the number down. Everything below is run at that mark.
Block 1 — CHOKED, your normal stroke length. Log makes out of 10 and the direction of every miss.
Block 2 — CHOKED, the pop stroke. Same mark, same target, same sitting: the stroke is the only thing that differs.

THE PACE CHECK, and it is the one nobody has run: 10 balls at full length and 10 at your mark, SAME stroke length, at a 15-foot target. How much shorter do the choked ones finish? That gap is what the 17-inches-past speed has to be re-learned against.
THE BLADE CHECK, once: set up choked and look at the sole. Flat is the pass. Toe off the ground means get a touch lower or stand a touch closer — this head balances to its lie.
Then the clip that is still owed: phone on the ground at ball height, square to the line, five putts. Shaft angle at ADDRESS against shaft angle at IMPACT — same number both times.
lesson.score: Makes pick the stroke; the pace gap is the number worth keeping. Carpet picks, the green decides — the 20-ball five-footer is still the real scoreboard and it has never been run on this putter. If you cannot say in inches how far down you gripped, the blocks are not comparable to each other or to next week.

viz.cap: Same hold, same choke — only the stroke changes

parts.t: mark the handle first — same choke on both

briefing.text: PUTTING — THE GRIP QUESTION IS CLOSED, and the claw is OUT. Your call, Sep 12 2026: you hated it, and you are choking up a little on the short ones instead. Conventional on every length. This item is no longer about a grip trial at all — it is the three things that are still owed, and two of them got SIMPLER when the claw went. (1) PUT A NUMBER ON THE CHOKE. Mark the handle, or measure down from the butt in inches and write it down. A shorter lever sends the same stroke length less far, so an unmeasured grip height is a pace variable drifting inside what you adopted as a line fix — and pace is the open fault. It also has to be identical on both blocks of the five-footer or that test has two variables in it. (2) THE FACE-ON CLIP, and it is ONE clip again rather than two: 240 fps, white tape on the shaft, shaft angle at ADDRESS against shaft angle at IMPACT. Vertical on both is the pass. The claw was briefly a second suspect for leaning the handle; with it gone the pop stroke is the only thing on the card that can deloft this 2° face, which is back to where the diagnosis was on Aug 25. (3) THE 20-BALL FIVE-FOOTER, choked down on both blocks, one with your normal stroke length and one with the pop. It has never been run on the LINK on any grip. Log makes out of 20, the direction of every miss, the green speed, and the choke you used. WHAT THE SPLIT STILL PROTECTS: full length on the handle past six feet, and if you are unsure which side of six you are on, it is a lag. NOTE the claw produced no measurement in either direction across its two days — it was adopted by decision and reversed by decision, and nothing in the record was built on it.

bay.setup: 78 shots · 13 clubs · 6 per club · Map My Bag
bay.finding: The first complete bag map exposed three things at once: a 4.8-yard 3w-to-5w overlap, a 25.3-yard fall from 5w to 2i, and an inverted middle-iron set in this sample. The detailed tables also confirm a leftward club path across woods and irons; TrackMan proves the delivery, not that an over-the-top body move caused it.

detail.gist: First full bag map: 78 shots, 13 clubs. The long end overlaps, the middle irons invert, and out-to-in delivery is radar-confirmed.
detail.story:
THE BAG MAP. Driver 195.8 · 3w 182.4 · 5w 177.6 · 2i 152.3 · 7i 135.9 · 6i 134.5 · 5i 128.3 · 8i 124.1 · PW 113.2 · 9i 110.2 · 50° 99.1 · 56° 84.5 · 60° 66.3. Those are the exact one-decimal averages TrackMan displayed, not rounded reconstructions.

THE LONG END. Driver to the TrackMan 3w label is 13.4 yards. The next gap is only 4.8 to the 5-wood, a practical overlap in this set, and then the ladder drops 25.3 to the 2-iron. The app does not silently decide that the 3w label is the Mini Driver; that mapping still needs the club name confirmed.

THE IRONS. The sample is inverted: 7i carried 135.9, 6i 134.5 and 5i 128.3. PW at 113.2 also crossed the 9i at 110.2. That does not prove the clubs are wrong—six shots apiece, with consistency of 12.5 to 18.2 yards through the 5i–7i, is exactly where strike quality can scramble a ladder. Retest the middle irons before making a bag decision.

THE DELIVERY. The driver club paths were −5.1, −6.9, −5.1, −9.6, −5.4 and −7.2 degrees: all leftward, averaging −6.6. The 6i was also leftward on all six, averaging −8.2, and the 8i did the same, averaging −7.6. That settles the delivery question for this session: out-to-in is measured. It does not settle why the body produced it; TrackMan cannot see posture or transition.

THE SHORT END. TrackMan consistency was tightest with the 60° at 4.1 yards, then 9i at 6.4, 56° at 7.0, and both 5w and PW/8i around 7.3–7.4. The wedge gaps were 14.1 yards from PW to 50°, 14.6 to 56°, and 18.2 to 60°.
detail.limits: Indoor mat, still air and venue balls. The Normalize toggle was on, but the recording did not show temperature or altitude, so these figures are preserved as bay offers rather than silently becoming the app's 70°F course carries. The balls were the lounge's plain unmarked balls; spin may be estimated, and carry is therefore a model built partly on a modelled input. Six shots per club is enough to expose a question, not enough to make an equipment verdict from an inverted gap.

briefing.text: TRACKMAN — next Map My Bag: photograph the settings page showing 70°F and sea level, and name the club TrackMan labels 3w. The Sep 14 session is fully stored, but those two facts decide whether its carry offers become the live course ladder and whether 182.4 belongs to the Mini Driver.
